Frame 0 shows only the background, and the first frame is the thumbnail on social players: have the title or key image already on screen at 0 s instead of entering from nothing; see references/review.md. @0s

Type floor is 28 px (2.6% of the 1080 px short side, what a phone can read) and 2 text elements stay under it for 0.5 s or more, the smallest "all generated from a single prompt" at 22 px: set reading text to at least 28 px, or put data-layout-ignore on text that is texture rather than reading; see references/look.md. @8.125s

"Just describe the motion" (4 words) is on screen 1.00 s (±0.01 s), under its 1.27 s floor: hold it about 0.5 s + 0.3 s a word (1.70 s here) before it leaves or changes; see references/motion.md. @12.172s

The film's last line "HyperFrames" (1 word) is on screen 1.04 s (±0.01 s), under the 2.00 s a closing line needs: hold it about 0.5 s + 0.3 s a word and at least 2 s before the film ends; see references/motion.md. @13.969s

The film's last line "is here." (2 words) is on screen 0.83 s (±0.01 s), under the 2.00 s a closing line needs: hold it about 0.5 s + 0.3 s a word and at least 2 s before the film ends; see references/motion.md. @14.172s

host id "graphics-layer", composition id "main-graphics" and file "main-graphics" differ. The hyperframes skill says this makes each render wait ~45s per scene; HyperFrames own shipped examples do it and hyperframes check does not flag it, so the render cost is unverified here. Matching them is safest
font-size 24px < minimum 28px for this format (ignore only for decorative micro-labels)
no hero object found (needs data-mh-hero, an MH.world instrument/3D/path/callout, media, or a diagram with >= 6 shapes): a scene of only text and flat blocks reads as sparse
scene uses no MH primitives (fine if hand-built, but check consistency)
45 tweens in one scene — is every movement meaningful?
no preview frames captured — any statement about appearance is source-based only
